name: Name

names.la-hawla: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah

meanings.la-ilaha-illallah: There is no god but Allah
meanings.subhanallahi-wa-bihamdih: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him
meanings.subhanallahil-azim: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him, glory be to Allah, the Almighty
meanings.salawat: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad
meanings.la-hawla: There is no power and no strength except with Allah
meanings.astaghfirullah-wa-atubu: I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance
meanings.hasbunallah: Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs
meanings.yunus: There is no god but You, glory be to You, I have indeed been among the wrongdoers
meanings.bismillah-protection: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing
meanings.audhu-bikalimat: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created
meanings.bismika-amutu: In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live
meanings.rabbana-atina: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire
meanings.astaghfiru-llah-x-allahumma: I seek the forgiveness of Allah (x3). O Allah, You are The Flawless and The Source of Peace, and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, full of Majesty and Honour.
meanings.allahumma-ainni-ala-dhikrika: O Allah, help me in remembering You, in being grateful to You, and in worshipping You in an excellent manner.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika: O Allah, I seek Your protection from miserliness and I seek Your protection from cowardice. I seek Your protection from being sent back to a miserable old age. I seek Your protection from the trials of the world and I seek Your protection from the punishment of the grave.
meanings.la-ilaha-illa-llahu: There is no god but Allah. He is Alone and He has no partner whatsoever. To Him Alone belong all sovereignty and all praise. He gives life and He gives death. He is over all things All-Powerful.
meanings.allahumma-ajirni-mina-n: O Allah, protect me from the Hell-fire.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asaluka-ilma: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, wholesome sustenance, and deeds which are accepted.
meanings.subhana-l-maliki-l: How perfect is the Sovereign, the Most Holy.
meanings.bismika-rabbi-wadatu-jambi: In Your Name my Lord, I lie down, and in Your Name, I rise. If You take my soul away then have mercy upon it, and if You return my soul then protect it with what you protect Your righteous servants with.
meanings.allahumma-qini-adhabaka-yawma: O Allah, protect me from Your punishment on the day You resurrect Your servants.
meanings.al-hamdu-li-llahi: All praise is for Allah, Who provided us food and drink and Who sufficed us and has sheltered us; for how many have none to suffice them or shelter them.
meanings.allahumma-innaka-khalaqta-nafsi: O Allah, verily You have created my soul and You shall take its life. To You Alone belongs its life and death. If You keep my soul alive then protect it, and if You take it away, then forgive it. O Allah, I ask You to grant me well-being.
meanings.bismillahi-wadatu-jambi-allahumma: In the Name of Allah, I lie down. O Allah, forgive my sins, ward off from me my shaytān, free me from my obligations (to others) and enter me into the loftiest assembly (of angels).
meanings.al-hamdu-li-llahi-2: All praise is for Allah Who has sufficed me and given me refuge. All praise is for Allah Who has fed me and given me drink. All praise is for Allah Who has been gracious to me and showered favours on me. O Allah, I ask You by Your Glory, save me from the Hell-Fire. (Ḥākim)
meanings.allahumma-bismika-amutu-wa: O Allah, solely in Your Name I die and I live.
meanings.al-hamdu-li-llahi-3: All praise is for Allah in every situation.
meanings.qaddara-llahu-wa-ma: Allah has decreed and He does whatever He wills.
meanings.allahumma-la-sahla-illa: O Allah, there is no ease except in that which You have made easy, and You make the difficulty easy when You wish.
meanings.inna-lillahi-wa-inna: To Allah we belong and unto Him is our return. O Allah, recompense me for my affliction and replace it for me with something better.
meanings.la-ilaha-illa-llahu-2: There is no god but Allah, the Supreme, The Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, Lord of the Noble Throne.
meanings.allahumma-kfinihim-bima-shita: O Allah, suffice me from them, with what You choose.
meanings.allahumma-inna-najaluka-fi: O Allah, we make You our shield against them and we seek refuge in You from their evil.
meanings.allahumma-anta-adudi-wa: O Allah, You are my aid and helper; by You I move, by You I attack, and by You I fight.
meanings.allahu-allahu-rabbi-la: Allah, Allah is my Lord, I do not assign anything as a partner to Him.
meanings.allahumma-stur-awratina-wa: O Allah, conceal our faults and assuage my fears.
meanings.allahumma-munzila-l-kitab: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, Defeater of the tribes, defeat them and grant us victory over them.
meanings.hasbiyallahu-wa-nimal-wakil: Allah is enough for me and He is the Best Protector.
meanings.allahumma-ahyini-ma-kanati: O Allah, let me live as long as life is better for me; and give me death when death is better for me.
meanings.allahumma-rahmataka-arju-fa: O Allah! Your Mercy is what I hope for so do not entrust me to myself for the blink of an eye, rectify all of my affairs. There is no god worthy of worship but You.
meanings.al-hamdu-li-llah: All praise is for Allah through whose blessing righteous actions are accomplished.
meanings.labbayk-inna-l-aysha: At Your service (O Allah!), the real life is the life of the Hereafter.
meanings.allahumma-la-tayra-illa: O Allah, there is no bad omen except what You bring and no good except what You bring. There is no deity other than You.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-2: O Allah, I seek Your protection from anxiety and grief. I seek Your protection from inability and laziness. I seek Your protection from cowardice and miserliness, and I seek Your protection from being overcome by debt and being overpowered by men.
meanings.ya-hayyu-ya-qayyum: O The Ever Living, The Sustainer of all. ; I seek assistance through Your mercy. Rectify all of my affairs and do not entrust me to myself for the blink of an eye.
meanings.allahumma-ma-amsa-bi: O Allah, all the favours that I or anyone from Your creation has received in the evening, are from You Alone. You have no partner. To You Alone belong all praise and all thanks.
meanings.amsayna-ala-fitrati-l: We have entered the evening upon the natural religion of Islam, the statement of pure faith (i.e. Shahādah), the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and upon the way of our father Ibrāhīm, who turned away from all that is false, having surrendered to Allah, and he was not of the polytheists. (Nasā’ī)
meanings.amsaytu-uthni-alayka-hamda: I have entered the evening praising You, and I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah.
meanings.allahumma-bika-amsayna-wa: O Allah, by You we have entered the evening and by You we enter upon the morning. By You, we live and we die, and to You is the resurrection/return.
meanings.hasbiya-allahu-la-ilaha: Allah is sufficient for me. There is no god worthy of worship except Him. I have placed my trust in Him only and He is the Lord of the Magnificent Throne.
meanings.raditu-bi-llahi-rabba: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islām as my religion and with Muhammad ﷺ as my Prophet.
meanings.rabbi-inni-zalamtu-nafsi: My Lord, I have certainly wronged myself, so forgive me. (28:16)
meanings.rabbana-zalamna-anfusana-wa: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be amongst the losers. (7:23)
meanings.anta-walliyyuna-fa-ghfir: You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are the best of those who forgive. (7:155)
meanings.rabbana-in-nana-amanna: Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire. (3:16)
meanings.rabbi-ghfir-wa-rham: My Lord, forgive and have mercy. You are the Best of those who are merciful. (23:118)
meanings.rabbi-inni-audhu-bika: My Lord, I seek Your protection from asking You anything about which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I shall be amongst the losers. (11:47)
meanings.rabbana-ghfir-lana-wa: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith. Do not put in our hearts any hatred toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are the Most Compassionate, the Ever-Merciful. (59:10)
meanings.rabbana-atmim-lana-nurana: Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are All-Powerful over everything. (66:08)
meanings.allahumma-innaka-affuwwun-karimun: O Allah, You are the Ever-Pardoning, the Generous; You love to pardon so pardon me.
meanings.allahumma-rabba-muhammad-ighfir: O Allah, Lord of Muḥammad forgive my sins, remove the anger of my heart and protect me from misleading trials.
meanings.allahumma-ghfir-li-dhambi: O Allah, forgive for me all of my sins: the minor and major, the first and the last, the public and the private.
meanings.allahumma-inni-zalamtu-nafsi: O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly and no one forgives sins except You; so grant me forgiveness from You and have mercy upon me. You are the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
meanings.allahumma-ghfir-li-war: O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, grant me wellbeing, guide me and grant me sustenance.
meanings.allahumma-ghfir-lil-muminina: O Allah, forgive the believing men and the believing women.
meanings.allahumma-ma-asbaha-bi: O Allah, all the favours that I or anyone from Your creation has received in the morning, are from You Alone. You have no partner. To You Alone belong all praise and all thanks.
meanings.asbahna-ala-fitrati-l: We have entered the morning upon the natural religion of Islam, the statement of pure faith (i.e. Shahādah), the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and upon the way of our father Ibrāhīm, who turned away from all that is false, having surrendered to Allah, and he was not of the polytheists.
meanings.asbahtu-uthni-alayka-hamda: I have entered the morning praising You, and I bear witness that there is no god worthy of worship but Allah.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asbahtu-ush: O Allah, I have entered the morning, and I call upon You, the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all creation, to bear witness that surely You are Allah. There is no god worthy of worship except You Alone. You have no partners, and that Muḥammad ﷺ is Your slave and Your Messenger.
meanings.allahumma-bika-asbahna-wa: O Allah, by You we have entered the morning and by You we enter upon the evening. By You, we live and we die, and to You is the resurrection.
meanings.subhana-llahi-wa-bi: Allah is free from imperfection and all praise is due to Him, (in ways) as numerous as all He has created, (as vast) as His pleasure, (as limitless) as the weight of His Throne, and (as endless) as the ink of His words.
meanings.al-hamdu-lillahi-lladhi: All praise is for Allah who has not taken a son, has no partner in His dominion and does not need anyone, out of weakness, to protect Him. (17:111)
meanings.al-hamdu-lillahi-lladhi-2: All praise is for Allah who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light. (6:1)
meanings.al-hamdu-lillahi-lladhi-3: All praise is for Allah who sent down the Book to His servant and did not place in it any crookedness. (18:1)
meanings.al-hamdu-lillahi-lladhi-4: All praise is for Allah, to whom belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth; and for Him is all praise in the Hereafter. He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware. (34:1)
meanings.al-hamdu-lillahi-fatiri: All praise is for Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who appoints the angels as messengers having wings, in twos, threes and fours. He adds to the creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is All-Powerful over everything. (35:1)
meanings.alhamdu-lillahi-rabbi-l: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, the All Merciful, the Very Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgement. There is no god worthy of worship except You, You do what You will. O Allah, You are Allah, there is no god worthy of worship except You. You are the Rich and Free of all needs whilst we are poor and in need of You.
meanings.al-hamdu-lillahi-hamdan: All praise is for Allah; praise which is abundant, pure, blessed and perpetual, as our Lord loves and is pleased with.
meanings.al-hamdu-lillahi-hamdan-2: All praise is for Allah; praise which is abundant, pure, blessed and perpetual, as our Lord loves to be praised and is appropiate for Him.
meanings.subhanaka-llahumma-wa-bi: How perfect are You O Allah, and all praise is Yours. Your name is most blessed, Your majesty is exalted and there is no god worthy of worship except You.
meanings.subhana-dhil-jabaruti-wal: How free from imperfection is the Owner of might, dominion, magnificence and greatness. (Nasā’ī)
meanings.subbuhun-quddusun-rabbul-malaikati: The Supremely Perfect, the Most Pure, the Lord of the angels and the Spirit (Jibrīl).
meanings.allahu-akbaru-kabira-wal: Allah is truly the Greatest. Praise be to Allah in abundance. Glory be to Allah in the morning and the evening.
meanings.la-ilaha-illa-llahul: There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, the One, the Supremely Powerful; Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in between them, the All-Mighty, the Most Forgiving.
meanings.la-ilaha-illa-llahu-3: There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne. There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of the Noble Throne. (Bukhārī)
meanings.la-ilaha-illa-llahu-4: There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, the Forbearing, the Most Generous. There is no god worthy of worship except Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Allah is free from imperfection, Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Magnificent Throne. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bi: O Allah, I seek protection in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your forgiveness from Your punishment. I seek protection from You through You. I cannot enumerate Your praise. You are as You have praised Yourself.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asaluka-bi: O Allah, I beg You as I bear witness that You are Allah, there is no god worthy of worship except You, the One, the Self-Sufficient Master, who has not given birth and was not born, and to whom none is equal.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asaluka-bi-2: O Allah, I beg You as all praise only belongs to You. There is no god worthy of worship except You, the Giver of all good, the Originator of the heavens and the earth. O Lord of Majesty and Honour, O the Ever Living, O the One who sustains and protects all that exists.
meanings.rabbana-zalamna-anfusana-wa-2: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves. If You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be amongst the losers. (7:23)
meanings.rabbana-amanna-fa-ghfir: Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us: You are the Best of those who are merciful. (23:109)
meanings.rabbi-ghfir-wa-rham-2: My Lord, forgive and have mercy. You are the Best of those who are merciful. (23:118)
meanings.rabbi-inni-audhu-bika-2: My Lord, I seek Your protection from asking You anything about which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I shall be amongst the losers. (11:47)
meanings.rabbi-b-ni-li: My Lord, build for me, near You, a house in Paradise. (66:11)
meanings.rabbana-srif-an-na: Our Lord, turn away from us the punishment of Hell-fire. Indeed, its punishment is endless. Indeed it is an evil residence and abode. (25:65-6)
meanings.rabbi-inni-lima-anzalta: My Lord, truly I am in dire need of any good which You may send me. (28:24)
meanings.rabbana-atina-mi-l: Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and provide us with guidance in our matter. (18:10)
meanings.rabbana-la-tuzigh-qulubana: Our Lord, do not let our hearts swerve from the truth after You have guided us, and bestow upon us mercy from Yourself. Surely, You, and You Alone are the Great Bestower. (3:8)
meanings.rabbi-zidni-ilma: My Lord, increase me in knowledge. (20:114)
meanings.rabbi-sh-shrah-li: My Lord, put my heart at peace for me, and make my task easy for me. (20:25-26)
meanings.rabbij-alni-muqima-s: My Lord, make me steadfast in salāh, and my offspring as well. Our Lord, accept my prayer. Our Lord, forgive me, my parents, and all the believers on the Day when the Reckoning will take place. (14:40-1)
meanings.rabbi-r-hamhuma-kama: My Lord, have mercy upon them (my parents) as they raised and nurtured me when I was young. (17:24)
meanings.rabbi-hab-li-mi: My Lord, grant me from Yourself pious offspring. Indeed, You hear all prayers. (3:38)
meanings.rabbi-hab-li-mina: My Lord, grant me (offspring) from amongst the righteous. (37:100)
meanings.rabbi-la-tadharni-farda: My Lord, do not leave me childless, though You are the best of inheritors. (21:89)
meanings.rabbana-hab-lana-min: Our Lord, grant us spouses and offspring who will be a joy to our eyes, and make us leaders of those who have taqwa (piety). (25:74)
meanings.rabbi-awzini-an-ashkura: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do good deeds that please You. And admit me by Your mercy amongst Your righteous servants. (27:19)
meanings.rabbi-awzini-an-ashkura-2: My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do good deeds that please You. Make my offspring righteous; I truly repent to you, and truly I am of those who submit to You. (46:15)
meanings.rabbi-audhu-bika-min: My Lord, I seek protection with You from the promptings of the devils; and I seek protection in You, my Lord, from their coming near me. (23:97-98)
meanings.rabbana-ghfir-lana-dhunubana: Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our extravagance in our affairs. Make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people. (3:147)
meanings.rabbana-afrigh-alayna-sabra: Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make our steps firm and grant us victory over the disbelieving people. (2:250)
meanings.rabbin-surni-ala-l: My Lord, support me against the people who spread corruption. (29:30)
meanings.rabbana-la-tajalna-maal: Our Lord, do not let us join the wrongdoing people. (7:47)
meanings.rabbana-la-tajalna-fitnata: Our Lord, do not make us victims of the oppressors. Save us, through Your mercy, from the disbelieving people. (10:85-6)
meanings.rabbana-alayka-tawakkalna-wa: Our Lord, in You Alone we trust, and to You Alone we turn, and to You is the ultimate return. Our Lord, do not let us be persecuted by those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed You, and only You, are the All-Mighty, the All-Wise. (60:4-5)
meanings.rabbi-anni-massaniya-d: (My Lord), indeed adversity has touched me, and you are the Most Merciful of the merciful. (21:83)
meanings.allahumma-ya-fatira-s: (O Allah), Originator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and in the Hereafter. Make me die a Muslim and join me with the righteous. (12:101)
meanings.rabbana-taqabbal-minna-innaka: Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You – and You alone – are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. And accept our repentance. Indeed, You -and You alone – are the Acceptor of repentance, the very Merciful. (2:127-8)
meanings.allahumma-salli-ala-muhammad: O Allah, honour and have mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You have honoured and had mercy upon the family of Ibrāhīm, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You have blessed the family of Ibrāhīm in the worlds. Indeed, You are the Most Praiseworthy, the Most Glorious.
meanings.allahumma-salli-ala-muhammad-2: O Allah, honour and have mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You have blessed Ibrāhīm in the worlds. Indeed, You are the Most Praiseworthy, the Most Glorious.
meanings.allahumma-salli-ala-muhammad-3: O Allah, honour and have mercy upon Muhammad, Your servant and Messenger, as You have honoured and had mercy upon the family of Ibrāhīm. Bless Muhammad and his household as You have blessed Ibrāhīm.
meanings.allahumma-salli-ala-muhammad-4: O Allah, honour and have mercy upon Muhammad and his household.
meanings.allahumma-innaka-affuwwun-tuhibb: O Allah, You are the Ever-Pardoning, You love to pardon so pardon me.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asaluka-imana: O Allah, I beg you for faith which does not waver, blessings which do not cease, and the company of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the loftiest abode of the Eternal Garden.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asalukal-firdawsa: O Allah, I beg you for al-Firdaws, the loftiest abode of Paradise.
meanings.allahumma-rabba-jabraila-wa: O Allah, Lord of Jabrā’īl and Mīkā’īl, and the Lord of Isrāfīl, I seek Your protection from the heat of the Hell-fire and from the punishment of the grave.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-3: O Allah, I seek Your protection from the punishment of the Hell-fire, and from the punishment of the grave, and from the trials of life and death, and from the evil of the tribulation of Dajjāl, the false Messiah.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-4: O Allah, I seek Your protection from the anguish of the world and the anguish of the Day of Judgement.
meanings.allahumma-inna-nasaluka-mujibati: O Allah, we beg You for all that which will necessitate Your mercy and the determination to do all that which will necessitate Your forgiveness; for protection from every sin and accomplishment of every good; for attainment of Paradise and for freedom from Hell-fire.
meanings.allahumma-hasibni-hisaba-y: O Allah, grant me an easy reckoning.
meanings.allahumma-atini-afdala-ma: O Allah, grant me the best of what You grant Your righteous slaves.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asaluka-shahadatan: O Allah, I beg you for martyrdom in Your path.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asaluka-ishata: O Allah, I beg you for a pure life, a good death, and a return (to You) which is neither humiliating nor disgraceful.
meanings.allahumma-jaddidi-l-imana: O Allah, keep faith rejuvenated in my heart.
meanings.ya-muqalliba-l-qulubi: O Allah, Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.
meanings.allahumma-musarrifa-l-qulubi: O Allah, Changer of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience.
meanings.ya-waliyyal-islami-wa: O Guardian of Islam and its followers, keep me firm on it (Islam) until I meet You.
meanings.allahumma-ahsin-aqibatana-fi: O Allah, grant us the best outcome in all of our affairs, and protect us from the humiliation of this world and the punishment of the hereafter.
meanings.allahumma-inni-asaluka-l: O Allah, I beg You for guidance, taqwā (piety), chastity and self-sufficiency.
meanings.allahumma-hdini-wa-saddidni: O Allah, guide me and grant me firmness. O Allah, I beg You for guidance and firmness (on the straight path).
meanings.allahumma-alhimni-rushdi-wa: O Allah, inspire me with sound guidance and protect me from the evil of my self.
meanings.allahumma-faqqihni-fi-d: O Allah, grant me a deep understanding of the religion.
meanings.allahumma-nfani-bima-allamtani: O Allah, benefit me with what you have taught me, teach me what will benefit me, and increase me in knowledge.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-5: O Allah, I seek Your protection from knowledge which does not benefit, actions which are not raised (to You), a heart which does not humble itself (in Your awe), and an utterance which is not accepted.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-6: O Allah, I seek Your protection from a prayer which does not benefit.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-7: O Allah, I seek Your protection from knowingly associating partners with You and seek Your forgiveness for unknowingly (doing so).
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-8: O Allah, I seek Your protection from miserliness and I seek Your protection from cowardice. I seek Your protection from being returned to the worst part of life (old age), I seek Your protection from the trials of the world, and I seek Your protection from the punishment of the grave.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-9: O Allah, I seek Your protection from the evil of what I have done, and from the evil of what I have not done.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-10: O Allah, I seek Your protection from the evil of my hearing, the evil of my sight, the evil of my tongue, the evil of my heart and the evil of my semen.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-11: O Allah, I seek Your protection from evil character, evil actions and evil desires.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-12: O Allah, I seek Your protection from the loss of Your favours, the removal of Your complete protection, Your sudden punishment and all that which may incur Your displeasure.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-13: O Allah, I seek Your protection from hunger, as it is indeed an evil companion and I seek Your protection from treachery, as it is an evil confidante.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-14: O Allah, I seek Your protection from bad days, bad nights, bad moments, bad companions, and from bad neighbours in (permanent) places of residence.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-15: O Allah, I seek Your protection from severe trials, wretchedness, bad fate and that my enemies rejoice in my misery.
meanings.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-16: O Allah, I seek Your protection from poverty, scarcity, humiliation; and I seek Your protection from oppressing or being oppressed.
meanings.allahumma-k-fini-bi: O Allah, suffice me with Your lawful against Your prohibited, and make me independent of all those besides You.
meanings.allahumma-qannini-bima-razaqtani: O Allah, make me content with what You have granted me, bless me in it and be a protector for me in that which is absent from me (i.e. family and wealth).
meanings.allahumma-ghfir-li-dhambi-2: O Allah, forgive my sins, make my home spacious and bless me in what You have granted me.
meanings.allahumma-zidna-wa-la: O Allah, grant us more and not less. Honour us and do not disgrace us. Grant us and do not deprive us. Favour us and do not favour others over us. Make us pleased with You and be pleased with us.
meanings.allahumma-ahsanta-khalqi-fa: O Allah, beautify my character as You have beautified my appearance.
meanings.allahumma-fa-ayyuma-abdi: O Allah, any believing servant whom I have cursed, make that a source of nearness to You on the Day of Judgement.
meanings.subhanaka-inni-zalamtu-nafsi: You are free from imperfection. I have wronged myself, so forgive me, because none but You can forgive sins.
meanings.aibuna-taibuna-abidun-li: Returning, repenting, worshipping and praising our Lord.
meanings.tawban-tawban-li-rabbina: Turning turning, to our Lord returning, not leaving behind any sin [unforgiven].
meanings.astawdiukumu-llaha-lladhi-la: I leave you in the care of Allah, who does not allow anything entrusted to Him to be lost.
meanings.astawdiu-llaha-dinaka-wa: I leave your religion, your trust and the last of your deeds in the care of Allah.
meanings.zawwadaka-llahu-t-taqwa: May Allah grant you Taqwa as your provision, and may He forgive your sin, and may He make goodness easy for you wherever you are.
meanings.allahumma-t-wi-lahu: O Allah, shorten the distance for him and make travel easy for him.
meanings.allahumma-thab-bithu-wa: O Allah, make him steady and make him a guide who is guided.
meanings.sammaa-samiun-bi-hamdi: A listener listened to our praising Allah (for) His goodly trial of us. Our Lord! accompany us, guard us and bestow upon us Your grace. I am a seeker of refuge in Allah from the Fire.

virtues.subhanallah:
Ka’b bin ‘Ujra (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as saying: “There are certain utterances, the repeaters of which or the performers of which at the end of every obligatory prayer will never be caused disappointment: ‘Subhānallah’ 33 times, ‘Alhamdulillah’ 33 times and ‘Allahu Akbar’ 34 times after every prayer.” (Muslim 596)

Fātimah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him for a servant. He ﷺ said: “Shall I not tell you of something that is better for you than that? When you go to sleep, say: ‘Subhānallah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times, and Allahu Akbar 34 times.’” (Bukhārī 3705)

Amr b. Shu’ayb narrates that from his father who narrates from his grandfather that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He who says ‘Subhānallāh’ 100 times before sunrise and 100 times before sunset, it will be better than 100 camels. He who says ‘Alhamdullilāh’ 100 times before sunrise and 100 times before sunset, it will be better than 100 horses on which he sends 100 warriors. He who says ‘Allāhu Akbar’ 100 times before sunrise and 100 times before sunset, it will be better than freeing 100 slaves.” (Nasā’ī in Sunan al-Kubrā 10657)

virtues.astaghfirullah:
Thawbān (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times. (Muslim 591)

Burdah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrated that we (the companions) were seated when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came. He said: “No morning has passed by except that I have sought Allah’s forgiveness in it a 100 times.” (Ṭabarānī: al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ 3879)
virtues.tahlil:
Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He who recites [La ilaha illallahu wahdahu] after every prayer will have all his sins forgiven even if they are as abundant as the foam of the sea.” (Muslim 597)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says [La ilaha illallahu wahdahu] when retiring to bed, all of his sins will be forgiven, even if they are as abundant as the foam of the sea.” (Nasā’ī)
virtues.la-ilaha-illallah: The Prophet ﷺ said that the best dhikr is La ilaha illallah, and the best dua is Alhamdulillah (Tirmidhi 3383).
virtues.subhanallahi-wa-bihamdih:
Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “He who recites [Subhanallahi wa bihamdih] in the morning and in the evening 100 times, will not be surpassed on the Day of Judgement by anyone with better deeds except the one who says the same words or more.” (Muslim 2692)

Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says [Subhanallahi wa bihamdih] 100 times a day, all of his sins will be forgiven, even if they are as abundant as the foam of the sea.” (Bukhārī 6405)

He ﷺ also said: “Whoever says سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِه, a palm-tree will be planted for him in Paradise.” (Tirmidhī 3464)
virtues.subhanallahil-azim: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There are two statements that are light on the tongue, heavy on the Scale and are beloved to the Most Merciful: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ ، سُبْحَانَ اللهِ الْعَظِيْم.” (Bukhārī 6682, Muslim 2694)
virtues.salawat: Zayd b. Khārijah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Send salawāt upon me and be persistent in du’ā.” (Nasā’ī in Sunan al-Sughrā 1291)
virtues.la-hawla: The Prophet ﷺ called it one of the treasures of Paradise (Bukhari 6384).
virtues.astaghfirullah-wa-atubu: Burdah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrated that we (the companions) were seated when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came. He said: “No morning has passed by except that I have sought Allah’s forgiveness in it a 100 times.” (Ṭabarānī: al-Muʿjam al-Awsaṭ 3879)
virtues.hasbunallah: Ibn ʿAbbās (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) narrated: “[Hasbunallahu wa ni’mal-wakil] was said by Ibrāhīm (‘alayhis-salām) when he was thrown into the fire; and it was said by Muhammad ﷺ when they (i.e. the hypocrites) said, ‘A great army is gathering against you, therefore, fear them,’ but it only increased their faith and they said: ‘Allah is Sufficient for us, and He is the Best Disposer (of affairs, for us).’” (3:173) (Bukhārī 4563)
virtues.yunus: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The supplication of Dhun-Nūn (Prophet Yūnus) when he supplicated, while in the belly of the whale was: [the dua of Yunus]. No Muslim man ever supplicates with it except that Allah answers his supplication.” (Tirmidhī 3505)
virtues.bismillah-protection:
Abān b. ʿUthmān narrated from ʿUthmān b. ʿAffān (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) who mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no servant who says [Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru] three times every morning and evening, except that nothing will harm him.”

Abān himself had been afflicted with a form of paralysis, so the man began to look at him. Abān said to him: “Why do you look at me? The ḥadīth is as I have narrated it to you, except that I did not recite it one day, and Allah brought about His decree upon me.” (Tirmidhī 3388)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says [Bismillahil-ladhi la yadurru] three times (in the evening), they will not be afflicted by a sudden calamity till the morning. And whoever says it three times in the morning, they will not be afflicted with a sudden calamity until the evening.” (Abū Dāwūd 5088)
virtues.audhu-bikalimat:
Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever recites [A’udhu bikalimatillah] three times in the evening will not be harmed by insect stings in that night.”

Suhayl (a narrator) said: “So our family used to learn it and they used to say it every night. A girl among them was stung, and she did not feel any pain.” (Tirmidhī 3604)

Khawlah bint Ḥākim (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) reported: “I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: ‘Whoever dismounts at a place and then says [A’udhu bikalimatillah], nothing will harm him until he sets off again from that place.’” (Muslim 2708)
virtues.bismika-amutu: Abū Dhar (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that whenever the Prophet ﷺ lay on his bed, he used to say: [Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya], and when he woke up he would say: ‘All praise is for Allah Who gave us life after having taken it from us and unto Him is the resurrection.’ (Bukhārī 6325)
virtues.rabbana-atina:
Anas (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would supplicate with [Rabbana atina]. (Bukhārī 4522)

In another narration, Qatāda (raḥimahullāh) asked Anas (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) which supplication the Messenger of Allah ﷺ frequently made. He said: “The supplication that the Prophet ﷺ made very frequently is [Rabbana atina].” He (Qatāda) said that whenever Anas had to supplicate he made this very supplication, and whenever he (intended) to make another supplication he (added) this supplication in it too. (Muslim 2690)

Some of the companions of Anas (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) requested him to supplicate for them. So he supplicated with this blessed supplication. He then said: “If Allah grants you that (good in this world and good in the Hereafter), then He has granted you ‘all’ goodness.” (Fatḥ al-Bārī)
virtues.astaghfiru-llah-x-allahumma: Thawbān (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and say this. (Muslim 591)
virtues.allahumma-ainni-ala-dhikrika:
Mu’ādh b. Jabal (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took him by the hand and he said, “O Mu’ādh, I swear by Allah that I love you. I swear by Allah that I love you. O Mu’ādh, I advise you not to forget supplicating after every prayer by saying: this. (Abū Dāwūd 1522)

Mu’ādh b. Jabal (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took me by the hand and he said, “O Mu’ādh, I swear by Allah that I love you. I swear by Allah that I love you. O Mu’ādh, I advise you not to forget supplicating after every prayer by saying: this. (Abū Dāwūd 1522)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika: ‘Amr b. Maymūn al-Awdī narrated that Sa’d (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) used to teach his sons the following words as a teacher teaches his students and he used to say that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge with Allah from them this at the end of every prayer. (Ibn Ḥibbān 2024)
virtues.la-ilaha-illa-llahu: Abū Dharr (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhā) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says this 10 times after Maghrib and Fajr, whilst sitting in the position of tashahhud and before moving, Allah will write 10 good deeds for him for each time he says it. (Likewise) He will forgive 10 sins and raise 10 stages for him. It will be a shield for him against all repulsive things and he will be guarded from Shaytān. No sin will be allowed to reach him that day (i.e. destroy him or invalidate his actions) except for shirk. He will be from the best of people in terms of actions, except for the one who recites it even more than him.” (Aḥmad 17990)
virtues.allahumma-ajirni-mina-n: Muslim b. Ḥārith al-Tamīmī (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ secretly said to him: “When you finish Maghrib, say this seven times. If you say that and then die during that night, it will be a protection for you. And after praying Fajr, say the same. If you die on that day, it will be a protection for you.” (Abū Dāwūd 5079)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asaluka-ilma:
Umm Salamah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ performed the Fajr ṣalāh, he would say this, when he said the salām. (Ibn Mājah 925)

Umm Salamah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ performed the fajr Salāh, he would say this while doing salām. (Ibn Mājah 925)
virtues.subhana-l-maliki-l: Ubayy b. Ka’b (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the Witr with three rak’ahs. In the first he would recite: [Sūrah al-A’la] in the second: [Sūrah al-Kafirun], and in the third: [Sūrah al-Ikhlas]. And he would say the Qunūt before bowing, and when he finished he would say this, and would raise and extend his voice the third time. (Nasā’ī 1699)
virtues.bismika-rabbi-wadatu-jambi: Abū Hurayra (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said: “When any of you goes to bed, he should shake out his bed with the inside of his waist sheet, for he does not know what has come on to it after him, and then he should say: this.” (Bukhārī 6320)
virtues.allahumma-qini-adhabaka-yawma: Hafsah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā), the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ narrates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to go to sleep, he put his right hand under his cheek and would then say this three times. (Abū Dāwūd 5045)
virtues.al-hamdu-li-llahi: Anas (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would retire to bed, he would say this. (Muslim 2715)
virtues.allahumma-innaka-khalaqta-nafsi: ʿAbdullah b. ʿUmar (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) narrates that he instructed a man to say this when going to sleep. The man asked him: ‘Did you hear this from ʿUmar?’ He replied: ‘Someone better than ʿUmar; from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.’ (Aḥmad 5502)
virtues.bismillahi-wadatu-jambi-allahumma: Abū al-Azhar al-Anmārī (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ retired to bed at night, he would say this. (Abū Dāwūd 5054)
virtues.al-hamdu-li-llahi-2: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says this when retiring to bed has praised Allah with all the praises of His entire creation.” (Hākim 2001)
virtues.allahumma-bismika-amutu-wa: Abū Dhar (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that whenever the Prophet ﷺ lay on his bed, he used to say: this, and when he woke up he would say: ‘All praise is for Allah Who gave us life after having taken it from us and unto Him is the resurrection.’ (Bukhārī 6325)
virtues.al-hamdu-li-llahi-3: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw anything which displeased him, he used to say this. (Ibn Mājah 3803, Ibn al-Sunnī 378)
virtues.qaddara-llahu-wa-ma: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than a weak believer, and there is good in everyone. Be keen on what benefits you and seek help from Allah, and do not give up. If anything afflicts you, do not say: ‘If I had done (something else), such and such would have happened.’ But say this, for (the utterance) ‘If’ provides an opening for the deeds of the devil.” (Muslim 2664)
virtues.allahumma-la-sahla-illa: Anas b. Malik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) ﷺ narrates that the Messenger of Allah said this. (Ibn Hibbān 2427, Ibn al-Sunnī 351)
virtues.inna-lillahi-wa-inna: Umm Salamah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, “There is no Muslim who is afflicted with a calamity, and then says what Allah has commanded him [the above supplication], except that Allah will recompense him with something better than it.” She says: “When Abū Salamah (her first husband) passed away, I said, ‘Which Muslim is better than Abū Salamah – the first household to migrate to the Messenger of Allah?’ I then said (the above duʿā’), and Allah recompensed me (by marrying me to) the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” (Muslim 918)
virtues.la-ilaha-illa-llahu-2: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would invoke Allah at the time of distress with this. (Bukhārī 6345, Muslim 2730)
virtues.allahumma-inna-najaluka-fi: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was apprehensive of [a group] of people, he would say: this. (Abū Dāwūd 1537)
virtues.allahumma-anta-adudi-wa: Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went on an expedition, he said this.” (Abū Dāwūd 2632)
virtues.allahu-allahu-rabbi-la: Asmā bint ʿUmays (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: “Shall I not teach you words for you to say in times of distress?” or “when in distress?”. He then said this. (Abū Dāwūd 1525)
virtues.allahumma-stur-awratina-wa: Abū Sa‘īd al-Khuḍrī (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates: “We (the Companions) said on the Day of Khandaq (Trenches): ‘O Messenger of Allah, is there anything we can say? For the hearts have reached the throats (out of fear).’ He ﷺ replied: ‘Yes! (Say) this.’ Abū Sa‘īd al-Khuḍrī says: ‘Allah, Mighty and Majestic destroyed the faces of the enemy with wind and Allah made them face defeat through wind.’” (Ahmad 10613)
virtues.allahumma-munzila-l-kitab: ʿAbdullāh b. Abī Awfā (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, on one of the days that he met the enemy, waited until the sun rose, the stood among the people and said: “O people, do not look forward to meeting the enemy, but ask Allah for well-being. When you meet them, be steadfast. And know that Paradise is under the shadow of swords.” Then he said this. (Bukhārī 3025)
virtues.hasbiyallahu-wa-nimal-wakil: Ibn ʿAbbās (radiy Allāhu ʿanhumā) said: “The last utterance of Ibrāhīm n when he was thrown into the fire was this.” (Bukhārī 4564)
virtues.allahumma-ahyini-ma-kanati: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you should wish for death because of a difficulty that befalls him. Rather he should say this.” (Bukhārī 5671, Muslim 2680)
virtues.allahumma-rahmataka-arju-fa: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The supplications for the one who is distressed are this.” (Abu Dāwud 5090)
virtues.al-hamdu-li-llah: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw anything which pleased him, he used to say this. (Ibn Mājah 3803, Ibn al-Sunnī 378)
virtues.labbayk-inna-l-aysha:
Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out towards the Khandaq (Trench) and saw the Muhajirīn (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers) digging the trench in the cold morning. They had no slaves to do that (work) for them. When the Prophet ﷺ saw their hardship and hunger, he said, ‘O Allah! The real life is the life of the Hereafter, so please forgive Ansar (Helpers) and the Muhajirīn (Emigrants).” They said in reply to him, “We are those who have given the Pledge of allegiances to Muhammad to observe Jihād as long as we live.” (Bukhārī 4099, Muslim 1805)

Ibn ‘Abbās (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhumā) narrated that the Messenger of Allah stood on (the plains of) Arafat and when he said: “Labbayk Allahumma labbayk (At Your service, O Allah, at Your service)”, he said: “Labbayk, innama-l-khayru khayru-l-ākhirah (At Your service (O Allah!), the real goodness is the goodness of the Hereafter).” (Ibn Khuzaymah 4/260)
virtues.allahumma-la-tayra-illa:
‘Abdullāh b. ‘Umar (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhumā) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Verily, the one who refrains from doing something because of an evil omen has practised shirk (polytheism).” The people asked him, “O Messenger of Allah, what is the expiation of that?” He answered, “It is that one of you says, this'” (Ahmad 2/220)

Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no ʿadwā (contagion) and no ṭiyarah (omen-seeking), but I like al-fa’l.” They asked, “What is al-fa’l?” He replied, “A good word.” (Bukhārī 5776, Muslim 2224)

In another narration: “It is a good word that one of you may (over)hear” (Muslim 2223)

Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no ʿadwā (contagion), no ṭiyarah (omen-seeking), no hāmah (seeking omens in birds), and no ṣafar (the belief that the month of Ṣafar is a bad omen for marriages, etc.), and run from the leper like you would from a lion. (Bukhārī, Muslim 2220)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “There is no truth in omens [lā ṭiyarah] and the best of it is al-fa’l (feeling of optimism upon hearing a good word).” (Bukhārī)

‘Abdullah b. ‘Abbas (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) narrated: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was optimistic and he did not see evil omens and he would become pleased by a good name.” (Ahmad 2328)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “An evil omen (tiyarah) is that which causes you to carry out an affair or that which turns you back from doing it.” (Ahmad 1824)

Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated: “When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a word, and he liked it, he said: We took your omen from your mouth. (Abu Dawud 3917)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-2: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrated that one day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the masjid. He saw a man from the Anṣār called Abū Umāmah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu). He ﷺ asked, “What is the matter? Why are you sitting in the mosque when it is not the time for prayer?” He replied, “Never-ending worries and debts, O Messenger of Allah.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then asked, “Shall I not teach you words by which, when you say them, Allah will remove your worries, and settle your debts?” He replied, “Yes of course, O Messenger of Allah.” He ﷺ said, “Say in the morning and evening this.” Abū Umāmah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) said, “Then I did that, and Allah removed my worries and settled my debts.” (Abū Dāwūd 1555)
virtues.ya-hayyu-ya-qayyum:
Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said to Fāṭimah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhā), “What is preventing you from (doing) what I am advising you; that you say this in the morning and evening?” (Nasā’ī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-l-Laylah 570)

Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said to Fāṭimah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhā), “What is preventing you from (doing) what I am advising you; that you say this in the morning and evening?” (Nasā’ī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-l-Laylah 570)
virtues.allahumma-ma-amsa-bi: ʿAbdullāh b. Ghannām (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says this in the morning has fulfilled his obligation to thank Allah for that day. And whoever says it in the evening has fulfilled his obligation for that night.” (Abū Dāwūd 5073)
virtues.amsayna-ala-fitrati-l: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abzā (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said this. (Aḥmad 15360)
virtues.amsaytu-uthni-alayka-hamda: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you enters the morning, they should say this three times. And when they enter the evening, they should say the same.” (Nasā’ī in Sunan al-Kubrā 10406)
virtues.allahumma-bika-amsayna-wa: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say this when he would enter the evening.” (Al-Adab al-Mufrad 1199)
virtues.hasbiya-allahu-la-ilaha: Abū al-Dardā’ (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: “Whoever recites this seven times in the morning and in the evening, Allah will suffice him in everything that concerns him in matters of this world and the next.” (Ibn al-Sunnī 71)
virtues.raditu-bi-llahi-rabba:
Thawbān (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah has promised that anyone who says this three times every morning and evening will be pleased on the Day of Judgement.” (Ahmad 18927)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says this in the morning, I guarantee that I will take hold of his hand until I enter him into Paradise.” (Tabarānī in Mu’jam al-Kabīr 838)

Abū Sa’īd al-Khudrī narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said (to him): Abū Sa’īd, whoever is pleased with Allah as his Lord, Islam as his religion and Muhammad as his Prophet will be guaranteed entry into Paradise. He (Abū Sa’īd) was amazed and said: O Messenger of Allah, repeat it for me. He (the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) did that and said: There is another act which elevates the position of a man in Paradise one hundred grades (higher), and the elevation between one grade and the other is equal to the height of the heaven from the earth. He (Abū Sa’īd) said: What is that act? He replied: Striving in the way of Allah! Striving in the way of Allah! (Muslim 1884)

Thawbān (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah has promised that anyone who says this three times every morning and evening will be pleased on the Day of Judgement.” (Aḥmad 18927)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says this in the morning, I guarantee that I will take hold of his hand until I enter him into Paradise.” (Ṭabarānī: al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr 838)

Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Abū Sa’īd, whoever is pleased with Allah as his Lord, Islam as his religion and Muḥammad as his Prophet will be guaranteed entry into Paradise.” He (Abū Saʿīd) was amazed and said: “O Messenger of Allah, repeat it for me.” He (the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) did that and then said: “There is another act which elevates the position of a man in Paradise one hundred grades (higher); and the distance between one grade and the other is like the distance between the sky and the earth.” He (Abū Saʿīd) said: “What is that act, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied: “Striving in the path of Allah! Striving in the path of Allah!” (Muslim 1884)
virtues.allahumma-innaka-affuwwun-karimun: ʿĀ’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrated: “I said: ‘O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, if I know when the Night of al-Qadr is, then what should I say in it?” He said: ‘Say: this.’” (Tirmidhī 3513)
virtues.allahumma-rabba-muhammad-ighfir: Muhammad b. Abī Bakr (raḥimahullāh) narrates that when ʿĀ’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) would become angry, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would stroke her nose and then say (to her): “O ʿUwaysh! Say: this.” (Ibn al-Sunnī 456)
virtues.allahumma-ghfir-li-dhambi: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say this in sujūd.” (Muslim 483)
virtues.allahumma-inni-zalamtu-nafsi: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates: “I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to teach me a du’ā so that I may invoke Allah with it in my salāh. He told me to say: this.” (Bukhārī 834)
virtues.allahumma-ghfir-li-war: ʿAbdullāh b. ʿAbbās (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā): “The Prophet ﷺ used to say this between the two prostrations.” (Abū Dāwūd 850)
virtues.allahumma-ghfir-lil-muminina:
Umm Salamah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says this everyday, he will receive a reward for every believer.” (Tabarānī in Muʿjam al-Kabīr 23/370)

ʿUbādah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever seeks forgiveness for the believing men and women, Allah will write a good deed for every believing man and woman.” (Tabarānī in Musnad al-Shāmiyyīn 2155)
virtues.allahumma-ma-asbaha-bi: ʿAbdullāh b. Ghannām (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says this in the morning has fulfilled his obligation to thank Allah for that day. And whoever says it in the evening has fulfilled his obligation for that night.” (Abū Dāwūd 5073)
virtues.asbahna-ala-fitrati-l: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Abzā (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ said this. (Aḥmad 15360)
virtues.asbahtu-uthni-alayka-hamda: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When one of you enters the morning, they should say this three times. And when they enter the evening, they should say the same.” (Nasā’ī in Sunan al-Kubrā 10331)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asbahtu-ush:
Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whosoever reads this in the morning or evening once, Allah frees a quarter of him from the Hell-fire. If he reads it twice, Allah frees half of him from the Hell-fire. If he reads it thrice, Allah frees three-quarters of him from the Hell-fire. And if he reads it four times, Allah (completely) frees him from the Hell-fire.” (Abū Dāwūd 5069)

Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever says the above in the morning, Allah will forgive the sins he commits in that day; and whoever says it in the evening, Allah will forgive the sins he commits in that night.” (Abū Dāwūd 5078)
virtues.allahumma-bika-asbahna-wa: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say this when he would enter the morning.” (Al-Adab al-Mufrad 1199)
virtues.subhana-llahi-wa-bi:
Juwayriyyah b. al-Ḥārith (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhā) reported: “The Prophet ﷺ left (my home) in the morning as I was busy in performing the dawn prayer. He came back in the forenoon and found me sitting there. He ﷺ asked: ‘Are you still in the same position as I left you?’ I replied in the affirmative. Thereupon the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘I recited four phrases three times after I left you. If everything that you have said today was put in the scales, this would outweigh it.’” (Muslim 2140, Abū Dāwūd 1503)

Juwayriyah bint al-Hārith (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) reported: “The Prophet ﷺ left (my home) in the morning as I was busy in performing the dawn prayer. He came back in the forenoon and found me sitting there. He ﷺ asked: ‘Are you still in the same position as I left you?’ I replied in the affirmative. Thereupon the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘I recited four phrases three times after I left you. If everything that you have said today was put in the scales, this would outweigh it.’” (Muslim 2140, Abū Dāwūd 1503)
virtues.alhamdu-lillahi-rabbi-l:
ʿĀ’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates: “The people complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ of a drought. So he ﷺ ordered for a pulpit and it was placed in his place of prayer. He then arranged a day for all the people to gather.

ʿĀ’isha says (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā): ‘The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out when the disk of the sun appeared. He sat on the pulpit and praised Allah and then said: “You have complained regarding the drought of your gardens and lack of rain for some time. Verily, Allah has commanded you to ask Him and promised to answer your prayers, then he said [the above with the addition of] “Send down rain upon us, and make what you send effective and far-reaching until some time.”

Then he ﷺ lifted his arms until we saw the whiteness under his armpit. He then turned his back towards the people and turned round his upper garment while his hands were raised. He then turned to the people and descended the pulpit. He performed two units of Salah. Allah then formed a cloud. There was a clap of thunder and a flash of lightening and it rained with the permission of Allah. He did not stay inside the Masjid until there were streams of water running.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw wetness on the peoples clothes, he smiled until his front teeth became visible. He then said: “I bear witness that Allah is over all things All-Powerful and I am the servant and Messenger of Allah.” (Ibn Ḥibbān 991)
virtues.al-hamdu-lillahi-hamdan: Rifa’ah b. Rafi (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) said: “I prayed behind the Prophet ﷺ and I sneezed and said: this. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished praying, he turned and asked: ‘Who is the one who spoke during the prayer?’ But no one said anything. Then he said it a second time: ‘Who is the one who spoke during the prayer?’ So Rifaʿah b. Rafiʿ b. ʿAfrah said: ‘It was me, O Messenger of Allah.’ He said: ‘I said: this The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, thirty-odd angels hastened to see which of them would take it up.’” (Nasā’ī 931)
virtues.al-hamdu-lillahi-hamdan-2: Anas b. Malik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) said: “I was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ in a gathering when a man came and greeted the Prophet ﷺ saying:’Assalamu alaykum wa rahmatullah.’ The Prophet ﷺ replied: ‘Wa alaykumus salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh’. When the man sat, he said this. The Prophet ﷺ asked: ‘What did you say?’ He then repeated what he said. The Prophet ﷺ said: ‘By the One in Whose hand is my soul, ten angels hastened in eagerness to write it (its reward). But they did not know how to write it until they took it up to the All Mighty. Then He said: ‘Write it as my servant said it.’” (Nasai in Sunan al-Kubra 7718, Ahmad 12612)
virtues.subhanaka-llahumma-wa-bi: Abū Saʿīd Khuḍrī (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated: “When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ got up to pray at night (for tahajjud prayer) he uttered the takbīr (الله أكبر) and then said: “this”. He then said: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ (There is no god but Allah) three times; and: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ كَبِيرًا (Allah is altogether great) three times. He then said: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ السَّمِيعِ الْعَلِيمِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ مِنْ هَمْزِهِ وَنَفْخِهِ وَنَفْثِهِ (I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing and All-Knowing from the accursed devil, from his evil whisper, from his blowing, and from his spitting.” He then recited (the Qur’an). (Abū Dāwūd 775)
virtues.subhana-dhil-jabaruti-wal: ‘Awf b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates: “I stood with the Prophet ﷺ. He started by using the siwāk and performing wuḍu, then he stood and prayed. He started reciting Al-Baqarah and he did not come to any verse that spoke of mercy but he paused and asked for mercy, and he did not come to any verse that spoke of punishment but he paused (and sought refuge with Allah from that). Then he bowed and he stayed bowing for as long as he had stood, and he said while bowing: this Then he prostrated for as long as he had bowed, saying while prostrating: this. Then he recited Āl Imrān, then another surah and another, doing that each time.” (Nasā’ī 1132)
virtues.subbuhun-quddusun-rabbul-malaikati: ʿA’ishah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say this in his ruku and sajdah.” (Muslim 487)
virtues.allahu-akbaru-kabira-wal: Ibn ‘Umar (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) narrates: “While we performing salah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), someone from among us said: this The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Who uttered such and such a word? A person among the people said: It was me (who recited these words), Messenger of Allah. He ﷺ said: “It (its utterance) surprised me, for the doors of heaven were opened for It.” Ibn ‘Umar (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) said: “I have not abandoned them (these words) since I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saying this.” (Muslim 601)
virtues.la-ilaha-illa-llahul: ʿA’ishah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates: “When the Messenger of Allah would turn in his sleep (at night), he would say this.” (Ibn Ḥibbān 5530)
virtues.la-ilaha-illa-llahu-3: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would invoke Allah at the time of distress with this (Bukhārī 6345, Muslim 2730)
virtues.la-ilaha-illa-llahu-4: Ali (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: “Shall I not teach you some words, which if you say, Allah will forgive your sins even if you were already forgiven? He said: “Say this.” (Ahmad 92/1)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bi: Alī b. Abī Ṭālib (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say this at the end of his witr Salah.” (Abū Dāwūd 1427, Tirmidhi 3566, Ibn Majah 1179) In another narration, it is narrated from Aisha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā): “I noticed that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was missing from his bed one night, so I went looking for him, and my hand touched the soles of his feet while he was prostrating with his feet upright. He was saying: [the above without the word إِنِّيْ].” (Muslim 486)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asaluka-bi: Buraydah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard a man saying this. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remarked: “By the One in Whose Hand is my life, He has certainly asked Allah with His Greatest Name; when He is supplicated by it, He responds, and when asked, He gives.” (Tirmidhī 3475)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asaluka-bi-2: Anas ibn Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and a man was offering salāh. The man then said this. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remarked: “He has certainly asked Allah with His Greatest Name; when He is supplicated by it, He responds, and when asked, He gives.” (Abū Dāwūd 1495)
virtues.allahumma-salli-ala-muhammad: Abū Masʿūd al-Anṣārī (raḍiy Allāhu ʿanhu) said: We were sitting in the company of Saʿīd b. ʿUbaydah when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to us. Bashīr b. Saʿd said: Allah has commanded us to send ṣalāh upon you. O Messenger of Allah! But how should we send salām upon you? He (the narrator) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept quiet (and we were so concerned over his silence) that we wished we had not asked him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said: “Say this.” (Muslim 405)
virtues.allahumma-salli-ala-muhammad-4: Zayd b. Khārijah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Send salawāt upon me and be persistent in du’ā.”(Nasā’ī in Sunan al-Sughrā 1291)
virtues.allahumma-innaka-affuwwun-tuhibb: ʿĀ’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrated: “I said: ‘O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, if I know when the Night of al-Qadr is, then what should I say in it?” He said: ‘Say: this.’” (Tirmidhī 3513)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asalukal-firdawsa:
Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the the Prophet ﷺ said, “Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, offers prayer perfectly and fasts the month of Ramadan, will rightfully be granted Paradise by Allah, no matter whether he fights in Allah’s Cause or remains in the land where he is born.” The people said, “O Messenger of Allah! Shall we inform the people of this good news?” He said, “Paradise has one-hundred grades which Allah has reserved for the warriors who fight in His Cause, and the distance between each of two grades is like the distance between the Heaven and the Earth. So, when you ask Allah (for something), ask for al-Firdaws which is the best and highest part of Paradise.” The sub-narrator added, “I think the Prophet ﷺ also said, ‘Above it (i.e. al-Firdaws) is the Throne of Beneficent (i.e. Allah), and from it originate the rivers of Paradise.”) (Bukhārī 2790)

Muʿādh b. Jabal (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When you ask Allah, ask for al-Firdaws (the highest level of Jannah).” (Tirmidhī 2530)
virtues.allahumma-rabba-jabraila-wa: ʿĀ’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said this. (Nasā’ī 5519)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-3: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When any one of you utters the tashahhud (in salah), he should seek refuge with Allah from four and should say this.” (Muslim 588)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-4: Sharīq al-Hawzānī (raḥimahullāh) narrates that I entered upon Aisha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) and I asked her: “With which supplication did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ begin his Salāh when he woke up at night?” She replied: “You have asked me regarding something which no one has asked me before.” When he woke up at night, he uttered: Allāhu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest) ten times, and uttered Alḥamdullillāh (All praise be to Allah) ten times, and said Subḥāna-llāhi wa bi ḥamdih. (Allah is free from imperfection, and all praise is due to Him.) ten times, and said: Subḥānal Malik al-Quddūs (How perfect is the Sovereign, the Most Holy) ten times, and asked Allah’s forgiveness ten times, and said: “There is no god but Allah” ten times, and then said: this ten times. He then began the Salāh. (Abū Dāwūd 5085)
virtues.allahumma-inna-nasaluka-mujibati: Abdullah b. Mas’ūd (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) says: “From the supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was: this. (Hākim 1/525)
virtues.allahumma-hasibni-hisaba-y:
ʿĀ’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates: “I said: ‘O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what is an easy reckoning?’ He said: ‘(An easy reckoning is) that Allah looks inside His book (of deeds) and pardons him, for one who his taken to task and interrogated on that Day, O ʿĀ’isha, will be destroyed. And anything that afflicts a Muslim, Allah will expiate his sins as much as the prick of a thorn.” (Ahmad 24215)

ʿĀ’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates: “Once the Prophet ﷺ said: ‘Whoever will be called to account (about his deeds on the Day of Resurrection) will surely be punished.’ I said: ‘Doesn’t Allah say: “He surely will receive an easy reckoning.” (84.8) The Prophet ﷺ replied, ‘This means only the presentation of the accounts but whoever will be taken to account and interrogated, will certainly be ruined.’ (Bukhārī 103)
virtues.allahumma-atini-afdala-ma: Sa’d (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that a man came for Salāh while Messenger of Allah ﷺ was performing Salāh. The man said this when he reached the row. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concluded the Salāh, he asked: “Who spoke just now?” The man said: “It was me O Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He ﷺ said: “Then your horse will be killed and you will be martyred in the path of Allah.” (Ibn Hibbān 1609)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asaluka-shahadatan:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever asks for martyrdom with sincerity will be ranked by Allah among the martyrs even if he died on his bed.” (Muslim 1909)

Zayd b. Aslam (raḥimahullāh) narrates that ʿUmar b. Khattab (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) would say this and add: “and death in the city of your beloved.” (Muwatta 1003)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asaluka-ishata: ʿAbdullāh b. Masʿūd (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the du’ā of the Prophet ﷺ in the two Eid’s was: this. He would also add: “O Allah, do not give us a sudden death, and do not take us unexpectedly, and do not hurry us from (fulfilling) a right or (making a) bequest. O Allah, we ask you for chastity, self-sufficiency, taqwā (fear), guidance, and a good-ending in this world and the Hereafter. And we seek refuge in you from doubt, opposing (the truth), ostentation and fame in your religion. O Turner of hearts, do not let our hearts deviate after you have guided us. Grant us Your mercy. You are indeed the Giver of all bounties.” (Tabarānī in Mu’jam al-Awsat 7572)
virtues.allahumma-jaddidi-l-imana: ʿAbdullāh b. ʿUmar (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed, īmān (faith) wears out in your hearts the way a piece of cloth wears out. So ask Allah to rejuvenate īmān (faith) in your hearts.” (Hākim 1/4)
virtues.ya-muqalliba-l-qulubi: Shahr bin Hawshab (raḥimahullāh) said: “I said to Umm Salamah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā): ‘O Mother of the Believers! What was the supplication that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said most frequently when he was with you?” She said: ‘The supplication he said most frequently was: ’this’” She said: ‘So I said: “O Messenger of Allah, why do you supplicate this so frequently this? He said: ‘O Umm Salamah! Verily, there is no human being except that his heart is between Two Fingers of the Fingers of Allah, so whomsoever He wills He makes steadfast, and whomever He wills He causes to deviate.’” (Tirmidhī 3522)
virtues.allahumma-musarrifa-l-qulubi: ʿAbdullāh b. ʿAmr (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhuma) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Verily, the hearts of the children of Adam, all of them, are between the two fingers of the Merciful as one heart. He directs them wherever He wills.” (Muslim 2654)
virtues.ya-waliyyal-islami-wa: Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say this. (Tabarānī in Mu’jam al-Awsat 653)
virtues.allahumma-ahsin-aqibatana-fi: Busr b. Abī Artāt (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ supplicate with this. (Aḥmad 17628)
virtues.allahumma-inni-asaluka-l: ʿAbdullāh b. Masʿūd (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to supplicate with this words. (Muslim 2721, Tirmidhi 3489)
virtues.allahumma-hdini-wa-saddidni: Ali (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: “Say: this and when you make a mention of guidance, keep in mind the (Straight) Path and when you consider the Straight (Path), keep in mind the straightness of the arrow.” (Muslim 2725)
virtues.allahumma-alhimni-rushdi-wa: ʿImrān b. Husayn (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated: “The Prophet ﷺ said to my father: ‘O Husayn, how many deities do you worship now?‘ He said: ‘Seven. Six in the earth, and one above the heavens.’ He ﷺ said: ‘So which of them do you take for your ardent requests and fears?’ He said: ‘The one above the heavens.’ He ﷺ said: ‘O Husayn, if you accept Islam, I would teach you two phrases that would benefit you.’” He (the narrator) said: “So when Husayn accepted Islam, he said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, teach me the two phrases you promised me.’ So he ﷺ said: this.” (Tirmidhī 3483)
virtues.allahumma-faqqihni-fi-d:
Ibn ‘Abbās (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) reported: “Once the Prophet (ﷺ) entered a lavatory and I placed water for his ablution. He asked, “Who placed it?” He was informed accordingly and so he said, “O Allah! Grant him (Ibn ‘Abbas) a deep understanding of the religion.”(Bukhārī 143)

In another narration Ibn ‘Abbās (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) reported: Once the Prophet ﷺ embraced me and said, “O Allah! Bestow on him the knowledge of the Book (Qur’an). ” (Bukhārī 75)
virtues.allahumma-nfani-bima-allamtani: Abū Hurayra (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: this. He then said: “All praise is due to Allah in every circumstance and I seek refuge in Allah from the condition of the people of the Hellfire.” (Tirmidhī 3599)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-5: Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say this. (Ahmad 13003)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-6: Anas b. Mālik (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say this. (Abū Dāwūd 1549)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-7:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O people, beware of this shirk, for it is more subtle than the footsteps of an ant.” The one whom Allah willed should speak asked him: “How can we beware of it when it is more subtle than the footsteps of an ant, O Messenger of Allah?” He replied: “Say this.” (Ahmad 3731)

Ma’qil b. Yasār (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated: “I walked with Abū Bakr Siddīq (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He ﷺ said: “O Abū Bakr! This shirk is more subtle than the footsteps of an ant.” Abū Bakr asked, “Is shirk not only when a person ascribes a partner with Allah?” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied: By the One in whose hands my life is, shirk is more subtle than the footsteps of an ant. Shall I not guide you towards something which if you say, it will remove it’s minor and major? He ﷺ said: “Say this.” (Al-Adab al-Mufrad 716, Ibn al-Sunnī 258)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-8: Saʿd b. Abī Waqqās (radiy Allāhū ‘anhu) would instruct (to seek refuge) about five things this and he would narrate it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ . (Bukhārī 6370)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-9: Farwā’ b. Nawfal reported: “I asked ‘Ā’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) about the supplication that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made. She said that he used to say: this.” (Muslim 2716)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-10: Shakal b. Ḥumayd (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, teach me a way of seeking refuge so that I may seek refuge by it. He (Shakal) said: ‘So he took my hand and said: ‘Say: this.’” (Tirmidhī 3492)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-11: Ziyād b. ʿIlāqah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated from his uncle, that he said: “The Prophet ﷺ used to say: this.” (Tirmidhī 3591)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-12: ʿAbdullah b. ʿUmar (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) reported that from the supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was this. (Muslim 2739, Abū Dāwūd 1545)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-13: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: this. (Nasā’ī 5468)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-14: ʿUqbah b. ʿĀmir (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say this. (Tabarānī 810)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-15: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to seek refuge with Allah from this. (Bukhārī 6347)
virtues.allahumma-inni-audhu-bika-16: Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say this. (Abū Dāwūd 1544)
virtues.allahumma-k-fini-bi: Alī (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated that a Mukatib came to him and said: “Indeed I am not capable of my Kitabah (a contract of manumission between a master and a slave according to which the slave is required to pay a certain sum of money during a specific time period in exchange for freedom) so aid me.” He said: “Should I not teach you words that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me? If you had a debt upon you similar to the mountain of Sīr, Allah would fulfill it for you. He said: ‘Say: this. (Tirmidhī 3563)
virtues.allahumma-qannini-bima-razaqtani: Ibn ʿAbbās (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ would supplicate with this. (Hākim 1/455)
virtues.allahumma-ghfir-li-dhambi-2: Saʿīd al-Jurayrī narrates that he heard ʿUbayd b. al-Qaʿqā’ (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) speaking to man from Banu Hanzalah who said: “A man stared at the Prophet ﷺ while he was performing salāh. He ﷺ then started saying this in his salāh.” (Ahmad 16599)
virtues.allahumma-zidna-wa-la: ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated: “When revelation came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, one could hear what sounded like the buzzing of bees before his face. One day revelation was coming to him, he faced the Qiblah, raised his hands and said: this. He ﷺ said: ‘Ten verses were revealed to me, whoever abides by them shall enter Paradise (and they are): ‘Successful indeed are the believers…’ until the completion of ten verses (23:1-10).’” (Tirmidhī 3173)
virtues.allahumma-ahsanta-khalqi-fa: ‘A’isha (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhā) narrates that the Prophet ﷺ would supplicate with this. (Ahmad 3823, 24392)
virtues.allahumma-fa-ayyuma-abdi:
Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say this. (Muslim 2601)

In another narration Abū Hurayrah (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “O Allah, I am only a human being. Whenever I scold, curse, or punish a Muslim man, then turn it into purification and mercy for him.” (Bukhārī 6000)
virtues.subhanaka-inni-zalamtu-nafsi: ʿAlī (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrates that he saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say this and laugh after that. I asked: Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at what are you laughing? He ﷺ replied: “Your Lord, Most High, is pleased with His servant when he says: ‘Forgive my sins’, knowing that no one forgives sins except Him. (Abū Dāwūd 2602)
virtues.tawban-tawban-li-rabbina: Ibn ʿAbbās (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) narrates that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from a journey and went to his family, he would say this. (Aḥmad 300)
virtues.astawdiukumu-llaha-lladhi-la: Abū Hurayrah (radiy Allāhū ‘anhu) said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bid me farewell and said this.” (Ibn Mājah 2825)
virtues.astawdiu-llaha-dinaka-wa:
Ibn ʿUmar (radiy Allāhū ‘anhumā) would say to a man if he intended to travel, “I bid you farewell as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would bid farewell. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would say this. (Tirmidhī 3443)

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Indeed when something is entrusted in the care of Allah, He protects it.” (Ibn Ḥibbān 2682)”
virtues.zawwadaka-llahu-t-taqwa: Anas (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) said: “A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: ‘I intend to undertake a journey, so give me provision. He said: ‘May Allah grant you taqwā as your provision’ He said: ‘Give me more.’ He said: ‘And may He forgive your sin.’ He said: ‘Give me more, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.’ He said: ‘And may He make goodness easy for you wherever you are.’” (Tirmidhī 3444)
virtues.allahumma-t-wi-lahu: Abū Hurayra (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported: A man said, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I intend to travel, so instruct me.” The Prophet ﷺ said, “You must be mindful of Allah and exalt him every time you ascend a height.” The man left and the Prophet said this. (Tirmidhī 3445)
virtues.allahumma-thab-bithu-wa: Jarīr b. ʿAbdullāh al-Bajalī (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) narrated: “From the time I embraced Islam, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not prevent me from seeing him, nor did he see me except that he would smile. I complained to the Prophet ﷺ that I could not keep steady on a horse. He hit me on the chest with his hand and said this. (Bukhārī 3036)
virtues.sammaa-samiun-bi-hamdi: Abū Hurayra (raḍiy Allāhu ‘anhu) reported that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out on a journey in the morning, he used to say this. (Muslim 7075)

explanations.la-ilaha-illallah: This is the word of tawhid, the core of Islam. It first denies every false god, then affirms Allah alone.
explanations.la-hawla: Nothing changes and no one has strength except through Allah. It is said when something feels too heavy, letting go of relying on your own strength.
explanations.yunus:
Ask Allah Through His Oneness

Calling upon Allah through His Oneness is one of the most powerful ways to make du’ā. The grief-stricken Prophet Yunus (a.s.) cried out to his Lord:

لا اله الا انت سبحانك اني كنت من الظالمين

The Prophet ﷺ said that no one supplicates with this du’a’ except that his supplication is accepted. And nobody supplicates with it except that Allah removes his difficulties. (Tirmidhi)

In this du’a, Yunus (a.s) asked Allah through the following steps (known as tawassul in Arabic):

1. Invoking the Oneness of Allah and affirming that no one deserves to be worshipped except Him.
2. Declaring Allah’s absolute perfection and negating any faults from Him.
3. Acknowledging one’s own wrongdoing.
explanations.bismillah-protection:
Brief Commentary

• This duʿā’ begins by saying, “In the Name of Allah” but does not specify what we are saying it for.
• In Arabic there is always a verb implied with “bismillāh.” For example, when we say bismillāh before eating, it means “In the name of Allah, I begin eating.” Similarly, when we say bismillāh before reciting, it means “In the name of Allah, I begin reciting.” Each time we say bismillāh, there is a verb implied based on the context.
• In this duʿā’, we are implying, “In the name of Allah I seek refuge”.
• In this duʿā’, we are not seeking refuge or help from Allah directly, but we are seeking it with His Name. Such is the magnificence of Allah, that even His Name alone is sufficient for protection!
• With the protection of Allah’s Name, nothing in the earth can harm you, whether it is a human, jinn, animal, electronic device, or anything else.
• With the protection of Allah’s Name, nothing in the sky can harm you, whether it is rain, wind, hurricane, lightning, or anything else.
